summary: Close the provider-neutral customer-service operational boundary with a privacy-safe unified inbox, durable reply intents, customer timeline, RLS and capability-aware release qualification over existing commerce aggregates.

impacts.evidence: Customer refs, conversations, messages, replies, assignments, SLA metadata and findings use organization/workspace scope, transaction-local scope settings and forced RLS.
CustomerRef is minimized, inbound text is sanitized and stored with digest, and raw provider payloads, credentials and unnecessary PII are excluded.
Customer-service summary, inbox, thread, timeline, inbound, reply, assignment and transition operations are additive OpenAPI contracts with regenerated SDKs.
No new public event contract is introduced; existing inbox/outbox and canonical commerce aggregates remain authoritative.
Provider-neutral customer-service models and read-only MCP access expose the same capability-safe vocabulary without provider branches.
Migration 000055 is expand-only, catalog-hashed, tenant-scoped and adds immutable message/assignment/SLA/attachment/finding history with bounded indexes.
Forced RLS, permission split, sanitization, append-only triggers, Idempotency-Key and fail-closed reply states protect customer content and outbound effects.
Public replies are distinct from internal notes and AI drafts; capability, approval and kill-switch policy remains required for remote writes.
Reply, assignment, transition and finding paths retain actor, correlation, digest, expected version and remote-state evidence through the existing audit boundary.
Remote thread/message uniqueness, reply idempotency, unknown delivery state and findings preserve replay safety and remote drift visibility.
The repository boundary accepts normalized inbound records and queues outbound intent; provider webhook verification, egress and credentialed delivery remain connector release gates.
Summary and UI expose backlog, unread, SLA breach, unknown delivery and quality counters; operational docs define recovery and kill-switch response.
Append-only history is retained, outbound can be disabled, unknown replies require receipt reconciliation and no destructive rollback rewrites customer history.
Core/API/repository tests, OpenAPI parity, migration/catalog gate, SDK generation, frontend checks and customer-service static qualification cover the repository boundary.
